guarantees.claim: key_init_d gets key_init when key_init_sel equals KEY_INIT_INPUT
key_init_d gets key_sideload when key_init_sel equals KEY_INIT_KEYMGR
key_init_d gets prd_clearing_key_init either when key_init_sel is KEY_INIT_CLEAR or any unmatched value due to default branch
guarantees.cond: key_init_sel == KEY_INIT_CLEAR or key_init_sel not in {KEY_INIT_INPUT, KEY_INIT_KEYMGR, KEY_INIT_CLEAR}

assumptions.claim: key_init_sel must always be one of the three specified one-hot values (KEY_INIT_INPUT, KEY_INIT_KEYMGR, KEY_INIT_CLEAR) and must not be X or simultaneously active; the unique case relies on mutual exclusivity
assumptions.risk: If key_init_sel assumes an illegal or multi‑bit value, synthesis may either optimize unpredictably or the simulator may emit a violation yet key_init_d could receive a wrong secret (e.g., key_init when clearing was expected), potentially leaking key material

assumptions.claim: key_init and key_sideload must be valid key material when selected; the mux does not check integrity or freshness
assumptions.risk: Feeding a zero or constant value instead of a genuine key breaks AES security and may cause deterministic weak outputs

assumptions.claim: prd_clearing_key_init must provide a high‑entropy pseudo‑random word suitable for clearing key material; the module does not verify randomness or toggle activity
assumptions.risk: If prd_clearing_key_init is constant or predictable, the key clearing is ineffective and residual key data may be recoverable

uncertain_points.claim: unique case without an explicit error handling or assertion allows silent fallback to the default clearing path if key_init_sel is corrupted or glitched; a fault injection could force a selection of KEY_INIT_INPUT when the controller intended KEY_INIT_CLEAR, reading out key material instead of wiping
uncertain_points.risk: Possible secret exposure if an attacker can influence key_init_sel to revert from CLEAR to INPUT during clear sequence

formal_sketch.consequent: unique case without an explicit error handling or assertion allows silent fallback to the default clearing path if key_init_sel is corrupted or glitched; a fault injection could force a selection of KEY_INIT_INPUT when the controller intend

uncertain_points.claim: Default case unconditionally outputs prd_clearing_key_init, but it is unclear if the design intends a 'safe clear' default or whether an abnormal selection should assert an error/mask; the current behavior could hide state machine errors
uncertain_points.risk: A stuck or misconfigured state machine might remain undetected, potentially leaving keys uncleared or misrouted

formal.antecedent: key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_INPUT && key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_KEYMGR && key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_CLEAR

formal_sketch.antecedent: key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_INPUT && key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_KEYMGR && key_init_sel != KEY_INIT_CLEAR

security_implications: This chunk directly steers raw key material (key_init, key_sideload) and clear pseudorandom data (prd_clearing_key_init) onto the key_init_d bus. The use of unique case without a side‑channel‑resistant implementation means that a fault on key_init_sel could expose the key by selecting INPUT instead of CLEAR. The default fallback to clearing may mask upstream FSM failures. The chunk relies on external validation of key_init_sel’s integrity; any tampering with this mux can result in secret exposure or incomplete key wipe.
